title: red_master_judge@1: one verdict and one claim for a red master, before any session starts a fix

story.i_want_to: a red master run to be judged once (culprit commit, class of failure) and the claim posted by control before any session reproduces it
story.so_that: sessions stop fixing the same red master in parallel, which on 2026-11-01 cost three sessions two duplicate fixes and their CI runs (KB b00f57c6)

rationale: US-48.15 ranked this fifth. KB b00f57c6's rule is that a session reads the channel for a claim first; a claim that exists before any session notices makes the rule a mechanism.

acceptance_criteria.description: Registry entry red_master_judge@1 with archetype :judge, triggered by a failed push run on the default branch of an enrolled repository, once per (repository, head sha).

The verdict carries the failing test ids, a class from a closed enum (date_or_time, flake, regression, infra, unknown) and a culprit commit or null; control validates each test id against the run's own failure list and drops any it does not contain.
Control, not the agent, writes one channel post under master-fix:<repo>:<head-short> naming the verdict and files one master-red issue; a second red run at the same head writes nothing.

The outcome row records human_override when the commit that turns master green touches none of the files the verdict's culprit touched, and duplicate_fixes as the number of PRs naming any of the failing tests opened after the post.

test_cases.name: one verdict per head
steps: deliver two failed runs at one head
expected_results: one dispatch, one post, one issue

test_cases.name: invented test ids are dropped
steps: verdict names a test absent from the run
expected_results: that id not in the post

test_cases.name: tenant isolation
expected_results: each tenant's channel carries only its own post

technical_notes: Revert versus fix-forward stays with chg's auto-revert and the humans; this judge only names and claims.
The master-red issue it files can be admitted by US-49.1's admit_labels.
